Pay rise analyser

What would a pay change do to your take-home?

Compare your salary above with a raise, promotion or job offer. Higher-rate tax, National Insurance and student loan all change how much you keep.

+£10,000 gross+£600 / month net

Moving from £39,000 to £49,000 changes your take-home by +£7,200 a year (+£600 a month). You keep 72% of the extra gross pay; the rest goes in Income Tax and National Insurance. Your next pound at the new salary is taxed at a combined 28%.

Frequently asked questions

How do I calculate hourly pay after tax?

Multiply your rate by weekly hours and 52 weeks to get annual pay, work out tax and NI, then divide the net figure back by the same hours. At £20.00 an hour for 37.5 hours you take home about £16.20 an hour.

How many hours are in a working year?

The calculator uses your weekly hours times 52. A 37.5-hour week gives 1,950 hours; a 40-hour week gives 2,080.

Is overtime taxed more?

No. Overtime is taxed as normal pay. It can push part of your income into a higher band, but only the pay above the threshold is taxed at the higher rate.

What if my hours vary?

Use your average weekly hours, or enter your expected annual earnings on the Annual tab. Tax is worked out on total annual pay.
